chunks: My father, ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain, and Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan, may Allāh have mercy on them, narrated from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Mughīrah, from ‘Abbās ibn ‘Āmir, from Aḥmad ibn Rizq Al-Ghamshāni, from Um Sa’īd Al-Aḥmasiyyah, who said:

I entered Madīnah and rented a donkey to go around the graves of the martyrs. I said, 'I must start by visiting the son of the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him), so I will enter upon him.' I delayed the renter a little, and he called out to me. Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said to me, 'What is this, O Um Sa’īd?' I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I rented a donkey to go around the graves of the martyrs.' He said, 'Shall I not inform you of the Master of the Martyrs?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Al-Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (peace be upon him).' I said, 'And indeed he is the Master of the Martyrs.' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Then what is for the one who visits him?' He said, 'A Hajj and an ‘Umrah, and of the good, this much and this much.'

key_terms.ابْنِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Son of the Messenger of God

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam Al-Husain (peace be upon him) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Ṣādiq (a.s.) elevates the status of Al-Ḥusain (a.s.) by identifying him as the 'Master of the Martyrs' (Sayyid al-Shuhada), thereby prioritizing his visitation over the general martyrs. The promise of 'Hajj and ‘Umrah' signifies the immense spiritual merit of this ziyarah, while the gesture 'from the goodness, thus and thus' (min al-khayr hakadha wa hakadha) is interpreted by scholars as indicating that the reward is abundant, comprehensive, and multiplies with each visit. This hadith underscores the central role of Imam al-Ḥusain in Shia devotional practice and the concept of intercessory merit through his grave.
